name: aws-l0-certificate
title: L0: the certificate, with its forms inline
kicker: A preview of HEART · 2 of 5 · HEART L0
html:
L0: the certificate, with its forms inline

# GET /clientcertificates/xmbiqp
# Accept: application/hal+json
# Accept-Profile: <https://w3id.org/heart-rise/hal-schema-forms>
# 200 OK
# ETag: "seq-1.hsf.L0"
# Cache-Control: no-cache
# Link: <https://w3id.org/heart-rise/hal-schema-forms>;
#   rel="profile"
clientCertificateId: xmbiqp
createdDate: 2015-12-08T18:02:16Z
description: test-client-cert-2
expirationDate: 2016-12-07T18:02:16Z
pemEncodedCertificate: |
  -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
  MIIC6DC...XuHVdZ5r27XRRXEjg==
  -----END CERTIFICATE-----
_links:
  self:
    href: /clientcertificates/xmbiqp
  curies:
    - name: clientcertificate
      href: /profiles/clientcertificate#{rel}
      templated: true
_forms:
  clientcertificate:update:
    title: Update
    _links:
      target:
        href: /clientcertificates/xmbiqp
    method: PATCH
    contentType: application/json
    schema:
      type: object
      required: [patchOperations]
      properties:
        patchOperations:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            properties:
              op:
                enum: [add, remove, replace, move, copy, test]
              path: {type: string, examples: [/description]}
              value: {type: string}
              from: {type: string}
  clientcertificate:delete:
    title: Delete
    _links:
      target:
        href: /clientcertificates/xmbiqp
    method: DELETE

MOCKUP · Today · L0 · L1 · L2 · Everything in one answer: correct, and repeated on every read.
say: Mockup. The certificate as a HEART resource at L0: AWS's state as is, plus each act as a form: target, method, content type and its JSON Schema, all in one answer. The relation names stay AWS's. The ETag lets an act carry If-Match, so a stale view gets 412 rather than a lost update. The update schema follows AWS's PatchOperation: op, path, value, from.
